title: Understanding SVD Output
text: The singular values in Sigma represent the variance captured by each principal component. The larger the singular value, the more variance that component captures.

title: Interpreting $$V_T$$
text: The matrix $$V_T$$ contains the principal components. Each row of $$V_T$$ represents a principal component direction in the original feature space.

title: Analyzing the Plots
text: Look at the orientation and spread of the data in each plot. Which plot seems to have a primary direction that matches the principal component directions given by $$V_T$$?

hintAnswer: The first principal component captures significantly more variance than the second.
